steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: covariate-adjusted vs naive model

steps.question: Which genes differ between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) adipose samples when the model adjusts for sex and age (~sex + age + condition), and how does this adjusted gene list and effect-size ranking compare to a naive model that ignores sex and age (~condition)?
acceptance_criteria: Fits DESeq2 with design ~ sex + age + condition on the filtered count matrix from T1S1, using raw Salmon-derived integer counts as input
Fits a second DESeq2 model with design ~ condition only, on the identical filtered count set, as the naive comparison
Extracts the condition (treated vs control) contrast from both models with independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction
Reports a full results table (log2FC, p-value, padj, base mean) per gene for both models, sorted by adjusted-model padj

Reports the number of genes significant at padj < 0.05 in each model and the overlap (Jaccard or simple intersection count) between the two gene lists, explicitly noting genes that lose or gain significance after adjustment
Includes an MA plot and a volcano plot (adjusted model) with top genes labeled
States the adjusted model as primary/reported result and the naive model as a sensitivity comparison, per the research question's explicit statement that groups are not matched on age

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on adjusted-model DE genes
caveats: With only 6 vs 6 samples the DE gene list may be short; if fewer than ~10-15 genes reach padj<0.05, report ORA results as exploratory and prefer the pre-ranked GSEA which uses the full ranked list

steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among the genes differentially expressed between treated and control adipose samples in the sex/age-adjusted DESeq2 model?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the adjusted-model (~sex + age + condition) DE results from T1S2 as input, ranking genes by DESeq2 test statistic or signed -log10(p) x sign(log2FC) for a pre-ranked GSEA, and separately runs over-representation analysis on genes at padj < 0.05

Tests against human Hallmark, GO Biological Process, Reactome, WikiPathways, and KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID gene sets staged for Homo sapiens in this environment, confirming gene symbol identifier space matches the HGNC symbols in the counts matrix before running

Reports enriched terms with FDR-adjusted q-values, collapsing GO's nested-hierarchy redundancy (e.g., via semantic similarity or simply reporting top non-redundant terms) rather than listing raw hit counts
States clearly that this is the pathway-level readout of the adjusted contrast, not the naive one, consistent with T1S2's primary model

steps.name: PPI network context for top adjusted DE genes
caveats: STRING links file is large (~83MB gzipped, 13.7M rows before high-confidence filtering) — filter to combined_score>=700 and to genes of interest early to keep this tractable
Every edge appears twice (once per direction) in the raw file; deduplicate before reporting edge counts
steps.question: Do the top genes differentially expressed between treated and control (adjusted for sex and age) form a connected functional interaction module in the human STRING protein-protein interaction network?
acceptance_criteria: Takes the top DE genes (e.g., padj < 0.05, or top 100 by adjusted p-value if fewer than 20 pass threshold) from T1S2's adjusted model
Joins STRING human protein IDs to gene symbols via the STRING protein.info file, then subsets the protein.links network to edges among these genes at combined_score >= 700

Reports the resulting subnetwork's node count, edge count, and whether it is more connected than expected by chance (e.g., simple permutation of random gene sets of the same size against the same background)
Visualizes the subnetwork and lists any hub genes (highest degree) as candidates for follow-up
States plainly if the DE list is too short (e.g., <5 genes) for a meaningful network test, and reports that limitation rather than forcing an analysis

plan.title: Adipose treated vs control DE adjusted for age and sex
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon-derived integer counts, 12000 genes x 13 columns => 12 samples + gene column) from human adipose tissue, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Metadata records sex (F/M) and age (years) per sample, and the design is explicitly stated as NOT matched on age between groups — age and possibly sex are candidate confounders of the treatment effect. A naive two-group DE test risks attributing age- or sex-driven variance to treatment. The plan therefore: (1) QC-filters and normalizes counts with DESeq2, (2) fits a covariate-adjusted DESeq2 model (~sex + age + condition) as the primary model, contrasting it against a naive (~condition)-only model to quantify how much the gene list and effect sizes shift when age/sex are accounted for, explicitly checking whether age is confounded with treatment group (e.g., near-complete separation) which would make adjustment unstable, (3) runs diagnostic checks (PCA/hierarchical clustering colored by condition, sex, age tertile) to visualize whether sex or age structure aligns with treatment groups, (4) performs pathway enrichment on the covariate-adjusted DE gene list using human pathway gene sets staged in this environment (Hallmark, GO BP, Reactome, WikiPathways, KEGG MEDICUS/BioCarta/PID — all human, HGNC symbols, matching the organism and gene-symbol identifier space of the counts matrix), and (5) builds a gene co-expression/PPI context view of the top adjusted DE genes using the STRING human network to flag any that cluster as an interacting module. No translational (drug/safety/PK) framing is requested in the research question, so those tracks are omitted.
